## First Verse 
<!--Put the first five lines of a poem by Lewis Carrol in this section!-->
"Just the place for a Snark!" the Bellman cried,  
As he landed his crew with care;  
Supporting each man on the top of the tide  
By a finger entwined in his hair.  

## Second Verse
<!--Put the first five lines of a poem by Robert Frost here!-->
Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,  
And sorry I could not travel both  
And be one traveler, long I stood  
And looked down one as far as I could  
To where it bent in the undergrowth;  

## Third Verse
<!--Put the first two verses of The Walrus and the Carpenter here!-->
"The sun was shining on the sea,  
      Shining with all his might:  
He did his very best to make  
      The billows smooth and bright —  
And this was odd, because it was  
      The middle of the night.  

The moon was shining sulkily,  
Because she thought the sun  
Had got no business to be there  
      After the day was done —  
"It's very rude of him," she said,  
"To come and spoil the fun."  

## Last Verse
<!--Put a short poem you created using chatGPT of 20 to 30 lines,here!-->
The night folds in like velvet hands,  
cupping the hush of the sleeping street.  
Lanterns sway in the breath of autumn,  
their gold spilling on cobblestones. 

A cat slips through the seam of shadow,  
its eyes twin coins of molten glass.  
Somewhere, a shutter sighs—  
a tired house turning in its dreams.  

I walk where the air tastes of rain,  
each step a ripple in the quiet.  
The moon leans low,  
listening to the slow pulse of the earth.

A moth flutters against the lamplight,  
drawn to a sun it will never touch.  
I think of the letters I never sent,  
their words still warm in my chest.  

The wind carries a scent of cedar,  
and with it, a memory—  
your voice, soft as the first snow,  
telling me the world is wide enough for us.  

But the street ends where the river begins,  
and the water takes the lantern’s glow,  
folding it into its dark, restless hands.
